codex_consult.feedback_summary: Codex (gpt-5.5 xhigh) responded substantively after ~50K tokens of analysis. Verdict: 'PASS is reasonable' with caveats. Five points raised: (1) Integration test sufficient for daemon-control contract, NOT full substitute for true manual sandbox-daemon verification of live codex launch path end-to-end. (2) ?? coalesce safe: neither-set returns undefined unchanged; both-set has claudeSessionId win (least-risky); subtle edge of empty-string claudeSessionId not falling back is acceptable since valid IDs are non-empty. (3) Dist regeneration directionally trustworthy but only proves call sites exist in artifact, not that live dev daemon is running that artifact; working tree is dirty with unrelated edits. (4) Pre-existing test failures genuinely unrelated; they fail in isolation too. (5) Minor race: if daemon restarted immediately after Codex thread creation but before the local webhook POST completes, /list could miss thread ID — manual live verification would increase confidence but not a blocker. Bottom line: 'PASS is reasonable, but I would phrase it as verified daemon/list behavior and compile artifact presence, not fully proven live Codex recovery after daemon restart.'
codex_consult.feedback_incorporated: Codex's nuance about AC5 incorporated as minor finding in all_findings (verification methodology note) and into AC5 success_criteria_results.details — making explicit that the integration test proves daemon-control-contract end-to-end with real auth, while live codex-CLI sandbox spawn was infeasible due to tool-policy hook write restrictions. The dirty-workspace concern is incorporated as a separate minor finding (verified the cycle's 4-line edit is correctly placed at runCodex.ts:710-713 distinct from unrelated pre-existing dirty-tree changes). The empty-string claudeSessionId edge case noted as acceptable (valid session IDs are non-empty UUIDs). Race condition acknowledged as not-a-blocker (mirror-pattern matches claude's existing fire-and-forget behavior; same race exists in claude path).
